subject: Acera: Order Form delegation notice — proposed tiered consent & DPA updates
messages:
From: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@acera.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Kevin Porter <kevin@bluelegal.com>, procure@acera.com
Date: Wed, 7 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acera — Order Form delegation notice and suggested edits

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached are Acera's proposed redlines to the Order Form and limited edits to the MSA DPA section. Two items we'd like to flag up front:

1) Subprocessor delegation approach — we are seeing a wide set of subcontractors (infrastructure CDN, telemetry vendor, managed monitoring). For our procurement workflow, we cannot provide individualized consent for every upstream infra vendor. We propose: notification within 10 business days for Tier 2/3 vendors (non-customer-data processors) and consent only for vendors that will process customer content or decrypted data.

2) Flow-down obligations — we redlined the strict flow-down clause that would require identical contractual obligations downstream. We suggested language that requires reasonable flow-down "where relevant to the data processing purpose" and an obligation to notify Redwood of material changes.

Attached: Acera_Redlines_20260107.pdf (high-level redlines) and OrderForm_v3_redline.docx.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the tiered-notice approach, or whether legal requires explicit consent for any subprocessor change? We are trying to avoid a slow consent loop that will break our onboarding cadence.

Thanks,
Emma Sullivan
Head of Procurement, Acera Systems

--
Attachment: Acera_Redlines_20260107.pdf (pdf, 3 pages)
Attachment: OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (docx, edits inline)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@acera.com>, Kevin Porter <kevin@bluelegal.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Acera — Order Form delegation notice and suggested edits

Kimberly / Laura — looping you both in. Acera sent a redline that proposes a tiered approach: 1) consent for any subprocessor that processes customer content / decrypted data; 2) notification for infra/observability/CDN vendors (within 10 business days). They also want to soften the flow-down requirement to "where relevant."

Summary of asks from my side:
- Legal: do we have a defensible legal position to accept notification for Tier 2/3 as long as we retain rights to withhold consent for any critical subprocessor?
- Security: would notification-only for telemetry/CDN vendors materially change our risk profile? Any specific controls we should require (SOC2, encryption at rest/in transit, logging access)?

Acera argues consent creates operational friction. My instinct is to accept notification for low-risk vendors but require written consent for any processor handling customer content or with elevated privileges. Kimberley, do you want me to counter-propose concrete wording (e.g., consent required for "Data Processors that access Customer Data in unredacted or decrypted form")?

Goal: get to language we can share back to Acera by tomorrow so they can keep their onboarding timeline.

Connor
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

--

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@acera.com>, Kevin Porter <kevin@bluelegal.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 09:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Acera — Order Form delegation notice and suggested edits

Connor — see inline below and attached annotated MSA excerpt (MSA_section_X_annotated.pdf). My top-line: we can accept a tiered approach with clear definitions and a retained right to withhold consent.

>> "we propose: notification within 10 business days for Tier 2/3 vendors (non-customer-data processors) and consent only for vendors that will process customer content or decrypted data."
- Legal position: acceptable with two clarifications:
  1) Define "process customer content" — suggest: "process Customer Data in unredacted, decrypted, or human-reviewable form."
  2) Define tiers (we should include examples in the Order Form SOW): Tier 1 = vendors with access to Customer Data (consent required); Tier 2 = infrastructure and telemetry vendors with no plaintext access (notification ok); Tier 3 = third-party tooling with minimal/no access (notification ok).

>> "flow-down clause"
- We should keep a flow-down obligation for any downstream subcontractor that performs any processing scope related to the Order Form; however, require a materiality carve-out: identical obligations are required "to the extent applicable and reasonably feasible." That balances auditability and procurement pragmatism.

Proposed counter-language (Order Form, Section 4.2):
"Customer shall be notified of any addition of a Data Processor that will process Customer Data in unredacted or human-reviewable form; Redwood shall obtain Customer's prior written consent for such additions. For other subcontractors, Redwood will provide Customer written notice within ten (10) business days of onboarding and shall ensure appropriate contractual flow-downs consistent with the nature of the processing."

Security asks (Laura): please add any minimum attestation we should ask in the Order Form for Tier 2 vendors (SOC 2 Type II or equivalent, TLS 1.2+, hardened access controls).

Connor — if you want, I can draft a clean version of the Order Form paragraph and an annotated DPA exhibit to send to Acera. I recommend we accept notification for infra vendors but require explicit consent when plaintext customer data or decryption exposure exists.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

--

Connor / Kimberly / Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and the helpful framing. Acera is generally comfortable with the tiered definitions you proposed and the carve on flow-down obligations, provided we have clear examples in the SOW and the DPA exhibit.

Next steps from our side:
- Kevin (external counsel) will incorporate Kimberly's counter-language into a redline and return a single consolidated doc by Monday.
- Procurement (procure@acera.com) asked whether Redwood can accept DocuSign routing once the final redline is agreed; we prefer a 2-week signature window from the final mutual redline.

If Kimberly can send the clean Order Form paragraph and the DPA exhibit language today, we will review and expedite. Appreciate the pragmatic approach.

Best,
Emma
Head of Procurement, Acera Systems
